notes: All 289 pieces are listed (b1-b289) in booklet build order and the per-type/colour counts match the parts list.
Page order: base (steps 1-27), Reichstag with both side towers (28-49), Deutsche Bahn Tower (50), TV tower shaft and sphere (51-52), Brandenburg Gate (53-61), TV tower antenna (62).

Fix: the Deutsche Bahn Tower's bottom piece (11203, inverted tile) cannot sit on the studless pin tile 2460, and the technic brick cannot sit on a tile's flat top. The booklet shows the 11203 placed upside down so its anti-studs face up and receive the 3700's studs, and the tile's pin enters its centre hole. So b158 and b159 now have rests_on [] and are connected through other_joins (b158-b50 pin join, b158-b159 stud/anti-stud join). The 87087 bricks still rest on b159 because the 3700 has real studs.

The booklet is line-art, so exact stud positions on the staggered black base were inferred. rests_on lists the pieces judged to lie directly beneath each piece; treat exact neighbours in the base as best-effort.
Pieces attached sideways onto 87609 side studs (front plates/tiles, Berlin label), or hung under other pieces, have rests_on [] and are described in other_joins.
The grille units (2x2 plate + two grille tiles) are clamped sideways onto the side studs of the 1x2 side-stud brick in each Reichstag side tower.
Pieces such as the 2x10 plate and the 1x10 strip on the Deutsche Bahn Tower attach through side studs of the 1x1 side-stud bricks; the exact face and stud mapping is an assumption.

TV tower: shaft is 5 white connectors with 4 black pins between them and a grey pin at each end. The cone sits on a 2x2 plate; the grey bar passes through it. The observation deck is dishes threaded on the white bar, which plugs into the shaft's top pin.

Brandenburg Gate: 12 two-high stacks of round plates (6 on each side group), topped by 8 green slopes and 2 green tiles. Two fences with 8 round plates carry 3 green tiles and a clip unit (green plate, 2 clip plates, jumper plate, clip tile) at the centre.
